original_test_intent: Verify the maximum capacity supported by each SMBIOS Type 7 cache instance, not merely its installed capacity, is encoded with the correct legacy or extended size and granularity and remains correct after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 7 records, bind by handle/level/designation, retain the legacy maximum-size word and any applicable Maximum Cache Size 2 field, decode unit/granularity and selector semantics, compare effective maximum capacity with the approved cache topology, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves per-cache maximum capacities, legacy/extended unit rules, expected relationship to installed size and reboot plan. Raw decoding and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Expected maximum capacity for every Type 7 handle/level
Applicable SMBIOS legacy Maximum Cache Size encoding, unit/granularity and extended-field selector semantics
Expected Maximum Cache Size 2 value when selected and minimum formatted length
Policy requiring installed capacity not to exceed maximum capacity
Validated raw/decoded parser plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not resize, flush, benchmark or reconfigure caches or firmware.
Preserve raw legacy word, unit/granularity bit, formatted length and extended size field; a normalized size string can hide an encoding defect.
Keep maximum supported capacity distinct from Installed Cache Size and validate only their approved inequality/relationship.
Bind every size to a Type 7 handle, cache level and Type 4 relationships so shared records are not double-counted as independent capacity.
Stop on invalid selector/length, ambiguous units, installed-greater-than-maximum, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Decode effective maximum cache capacity per Type 7 handle from raw legacy/extended fields, validate units/topology and compare before/after reboot.
Do not substitute installed or OS-reported cache size, change cache state or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve maximum-capacity baseline, legacy/extended encoding and installed-size relationship.
Approve topology/reboot recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is relevant, but grep loses raw granularity and extended-selection data plus the handle/level context needed to interpret a normalized size.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 7 records, retain legacy maximum-size encoding and applicable Maximum Cache Size 2, compute bytes with version/length guards and bind by handle/level.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Maximum Cache Size scope, Type 7 script and 5/5-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the legacy capacity value and granularity, follow the specified extended-field selector when applicable, preserve both raw representations and compare the effective maximum bytes per cache handle with topology and installed-size constraints.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 7 systems, including cache sizes that require extended fields.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, Type 7 formatted length, BIOS, CPU/cache topology and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 7 Maximum Cache Size and Maximum Cache Size 2 encoding semantics, approved processor/cache topology and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds raw unit/selector/extended-field proof and separates maximum supported from installed capacity.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; detects unit, truncation and selector defects hidden by a decoded size line.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Per-cache maximum baseline and encoding policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS cache size usually describes usable/installed capacity and cannot by itself validate this maximum-capacity metadata field.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve handle-specific maximum capacities and shared-cache representation, but must express values with encoding/version provenance and cannot replace maximum with installed or OS-visible size.
expected_evidence: Approved maximum-capacity map, size encoding/selector rules, topology and parser versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 7 table with handle/level, formatted length, raw legacy/granularity and extended values plus effective bytes
Comparison with expected maximum and Installed Cache Size relationship
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot raw comparison
Engineer verdict with any specification-based unknown/not-applicable disposition

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and criterion consistently target maximum cache capacity; encoding and expected values are project/specification inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The legacy and extended fields are safely readable and machine-decodable once version and baseline are supplied.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds raw unit/granularity, extended selection, cache identity and maximum-versus-installed semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains topology/unit awareness while strengthening field encoding evidence and correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Prevents a decoder-normalized or OS installed size from replacing the actual maximum-capacity source field.

review_improvement: Detects capacity values that look numerically correct after decoding but are encoded with the wrong granularity or selector and preserves maximum-capacity intent.
independent_technical_reasoning: With an approved maximum map and encoding rules, raw extraction, effective-byte calculation, relational checks and reboot comparison are deterministic software tasks.
